question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.defaults.compaction.enabled: false` as a public configuration option whose scope is limited to proactive embedded auto-compaction, while overflow recovery, preemptive handling, and manual `/compact` remain active?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically narrow and the documentation makes the limitation explicit, but choosing this public configuration surface and its permanent operator semantics is a maintainer product-contract decision.

options.title: Accept the scoped configuration contract
options.body: Merge the additive boolean with the documented semantics, giving operators a supported way to disable proactive embedded auto-compaction while preserving recovery paths.

options.title: Choose a different control surface
options.body: Pause this PR and define a different supported configuration or mode contract if `enabled` should disable a broader or differently scoped set of compaction behaviors.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped configuration contract
recommendation.body: Merge the additive boolean with the documented semantics, giving operators a supported way to disable proactive embedded auto-compaction while preserving recovery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They can clarify the intended behavior and update the branch, but maintainer approval is still required for the permanent public contract.
